analytic.title: Embedded Real-Time System Modeling and Analysis Using AADL

div.p: Embedded real-time system has requirements for nonfunctional features such as schedulability, dependability and safety. With traditional design and development methodology these nonfunctional features could only be analyzed after the system is fully implemented. Architecture Analysis and Design Language (AADL) is a modeling language that supports early and repeated analyses of a system's architecture with respect to performance-critical properties through an extendable notation, a tool framework, and precisely defined semantics. AADL can be used in the analysis of partially defined architectural patterns with limited architectural detail, it is suitable for team work in large-scale system design and development. Avionic Air Data System is used as the AADL modeling and analysis study case. A basic model with software, hardware components is created.
Software components are allocated to hardware components.
Resource budget analysis, resource allocation analysis and end to end flow latency analysis are performed on Air Data system.

Part of system model is redesigned depends on the analysis results. All these analyses are performed in the early phase of system design and development. It helps to find out issues early to save costs and reduce potential errors.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: Embedded real-time systems, especially safety-critical system such as avionic system, space application and automotive application, have requirements for schedulability, dependability, safety. As the complexity of embedded system increases, it becomes more challenge to design embedded real-time system. Besides functional features, nonfunctional features are also key requirements for embedded real-time system. All these nonfunctional features should be analyzed at the initial phase of system development so that potential issues could be found out early to save costs and reduce potential errors [1].

Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) is the formalized application of modeling to support system requirements, design, analysis, verification and validation activities beginning in the conceptual design phase and continuing throughout development and later life cycle phases. MBSE is a methodology which could create an abstract system model at early design phase for nonfunctional feature analysis [2]. The main advantage of 978-1-4244-7578-0/$26.00 © 2010 IEEE the MBSE is that model can be analyzed and tested in order to find design and implementation errors [3].

The Society of Automotive Engineers Architecture Analysis and Design Language (AADL) is a MBSE supported modeling language that supports early and repeated analyses of a system's architecture with respect to performance-critical properties through an extendable notation, a tool framework, and precisely defined semantics [4]. Besides, AADL is suitable for embedded real-time system modeling since it allows deploying software models on different hardware resources for reconfigurable distributed control applications [5].

The rest of this paper is structured as follows. Section II provides a brief introduction to the AADL and why AADL is suitable for embedded real-time system modeling and analysis. Section III describes the case study in this research work, Avionic Air Data System. Section IV develops AADL model for Avionic Air Data System. Section V presents the analysis of Air Data System AADL model. Section VI presents AADL partial specification and AADL in large scale system development. Section VII draws conclusions from this work, as well as insights into future directions.

div.head: II. ARCHITECTURE ANALYSIS AND DESIGN LANGUAGE
div.p: AADL was developed by the international Society of Automotive Engineers (SAE). The language employs formal modeling concepts for the description and analysis of application system architectures in terms of distinct components and their interactions. It includes abstractions of software, computational hardware, and system components for (a) specifying and analyzing embedded real-time and high dependability systems, complex systems of systems, and specialized performance capability systems and (b) mapping of software onto computational hardware elements [6]. The AADL is especially effective for model-based analysis and specification of complex embedded real-time systems.
The AADL can be used to model and analyze systems already in use and design and integrate new systems.
AADL represents system with components. AADL components are divided into three categories [6]:
• Application Software: Thread, Thread Group, Process, Data, Subprogram.

• Hardware Platform: Processor, Memory, Device, Bus. • explicit access to data components Each AADL component has some performance-critical properties binding on it. With these properties AADL tools could analyze the system nonfunctional features such as resource consumption, end to end flow latency, schedulability, dependability and safety. By utilizing the extension capabilities of the language, additional models and properties can be included so that analysis could be done for other features.

The AADL can be used in the analysis of partially defined architectural patterns (with limited architectural detail) as well as in full-scale analysis of a complete system model extracted from the source code (with completely quantified system property values). Air Data System provides real-time flight information to pilot and other control system. It has a demand for the fast response time, high dependability.

div.head: IV. AADL MODELING OF AVIONIC AIR DATA SYSTEM
A. Software Components
div.p: Both software and hardware components are modeled for Air Data System. Fig. 3 shows application software system consistes of AirDataManager(AD), DisplayManager(DM), WingFlapManager(WFM) and AirInletManager(AIM) process components.

div.head: B. Hardware Components
div.p: Two hardware system models are created to provide different solutions. One is a low-end hardware platform which conations weak processing capacity processor, low speed bus, small size RAM memory and ROM memory. The other is high performance hardware platform which consists of strong processing capacity processor, high speed bus, big SIze RAM memory and ROM memory. These two hardware models provide execution platforms for AirDataManager, DisplayManger, WingFlapManager and AirInlentManger processes.
Pressure Sensor, Temperature Sensor, Angle of Attack Sensor and Pilot Display are modeled as devices.

Data port connections are established between software components and devices for data transfer. Since there are two kinds of hardware platforms, two allocation solutions are provided. With low-end hardware platform, each software process is allocated to one standalone hardware for enough processing capacity. With high performance hardware platform, all the software processes are allocated to one hardware platform. System use ARINC 653 partitions which work as virtual machines to make space and time partitioning [8]. A partition has an address space boundary. Process in one partition could not overwrite data in other partitions. A partition is guaranteed a specified amount of real processor time, so that process failure in one partition does not affect processes of other partitions on the same hardware. Each partition seems like a standalone hardware platform.

div.head: A. Resource Budget Analysis
div.p: Resource budget analysis is used in the early phase of design to provide budgeting support. Only partial designed software model and simple hardware platform which consists of some processors, memory and bus are created at this phase. Processor has a MIPSCapacity property which shows the execution capacity in million instructions per second (MIPS). RAM memory has RAMCapacity property which represents the RAM memory size. Similarly ROM memory has ROMCapacity property which represents the ROM memory size. Application software components represent their processor, memory and bus requirements through MIPSBudget, RAMBudget, ROMBudget properties. Table I shows the resource capacity and budget of Air Data System model.

Resource budget analysis only add all the hardware resource capacity together, add up all the software resource budget, and check whether the total hardware resource capacity meet the total software resource budget. For budget analysis in Table I, total low-end hardware capacity could meet total software budget, but total high performance hardware capacity could not meet total software budget.

However, both low-end hardware platform and high performance hardware platform provide very big RAM and ROM memory sizes which exceed software budget a lot. For the low-end platform, RAM size is 4000, software RAM budget is 600. The RAM utilization rate is 15%. ROM utilization rate is 10%. Smaller RAM and ROM memories could be considered to improve resource utilization.

div.head: B. Resource Allocation Analysis
div.p: Total hardware capacity meet total software budget does not mean the hardware platform could support the application software. Each application software component must be allocated to a specific processor or memory. Resource allocation analysis takes into consideration the allocation of application software component to hardware platform.

Consider the data in Table I, if processor budget of AirDataManger is 1200, when allocate all the four software components to low-end platform with four independent low end processors, resource budget analysis reports ok since total processor capacity (1000*4) exceed total processor budget (1200+500+500+50). However, resource allocation analysis will report error since AirDataManger processor budget (1200) exceeds a single low-end processor capacity (1000).

Resource allocation analysis could help to find out issues in current system design. With these analysis results, ref actor could be done to optimize the system model and allocation. As described in Section IV, two kinds of hardware platforms are provided for Air Data System. div.head: C. End to End Latency Analysis
div.p: Avionic Air Data System is an embedded real-time system which has a demand for real-time response. Flow could be added to AADL component to express a logical path within the component from input port to output port. Each AADL flow could have a Latency property to indicate the time for data passing through the flow. Connections between processes could also have Latency property to indicate time transferring data between process components. For partitions components Partition_Latency is added to indicate time latency for cross-partition data transfer. End to end latency analysis take into account all the latency value involved in end to end flow including process latency, connection latency and partition latency.

In Air Data System, the response time is calculated on end to end flow from sensors to AirDataManager, and sequentially to DisplayManager, finally to PiiotDisplay. Fig. 4 shows the end to end data flow of Air Data System. Both AirDataManager and DisplayManager processes have flows with latency properties. Connections between components also have latency properties binding on them.

The end to end flow latency result is a worst-case end-to end flow latency. The analysis result could help to find the bottle neck of flow latency, and lead to appropriate system model refactoring. If latency analysis result exceeds the requirements a lot, system architecture should be considered to be redesigned. For example, prefer more powerful hardware for better data processing capacity and communication speed. If latency result almost meets the requirement, application software adjustment could be considered to get better performance to meet latency requirement. For example, use more efficient algorithm for better performance [10].

As showed in FigA, AirDataManager has five input data from four different devices. All these input data are generated independently. AirDataManager use a periodic 10 thread to group all these input data together, and send them to other data processing threads in AirDataManager periodically. The flow latency from sensors to AirDataManager depends on periodic 10 thread's period. II shows end to end flow latency result of Air Data System prototype from AirDataManager to PiiotDisplay. From the latency result of system, connection delay is the main factor of the end to end latency. Improvement of application software will be futile for faster response time. Two appropriate refactoring solutions could be done to meet the expec�ed flow latency. First solution is replacing current connectIOn bus with high speed bus for faster connection data transfer rate. Second solution is allocating applications to one processor so that connection delay between these components could be minimized.

div.head: VI. AADL IN LARGE-SCALE SYSTEM DEVELOPMENT
div.p: AADL supports partial specification which means analysis could be done on the partial designed model. This feature makes AADL a useful tool for coordinating in large scale system design and development. System architect could create a partial model at an abstract level, with only general design including interfaces and properties � f subsystems and connections betwee� su�sys!ems. T?IS general design does not contain any detati . deslgn mformatl � n of subsystem except interface and properties. AADL analYSIS could be done on this general designed model as early phase analysis. Different subsystem architects will create subsystem models with detailed subsystem design based on the subsystem interface and properties. A full-scale AADL analysis of system could be done when all subsystems are merged into system.

In Section IV, Air Data System model was created only at process level. All the analysis in Sect�on V . was b � sed on the general designed model. As descnbed m SectIOn III, AirDataManager subsystem could be designed at thread level with more details. Fig. 5 shows the AirDataManager subsystem AADL model. Periodic 10 thread is not presented here in the figure for a brief view. Resource budget analysis, resource allocation analysis, end to end flow latency analysis could be done at thread level to verify subsystem design meet system requirements. Other subsystems such as DisplayManger, WingFlapManager, AirInletManager could also be modeled and analyzed like AirDataManager.

div.head: VII. CONCLUSION
div.p: The AADL can be used to model and analyze systems already in use and design and integrate new systems. AADL supports the early prediction and analysis of embedded real time system nonfunctional features such as schedulability, reliability and safety. Avionic Air Data System was modeled and analyzed using AADL in this research. With the resource budget and resource allocation analysis result, system was redesigned to meet the system requirements. End to end latency analysis result was used to check system response time to meet the real-time requirement. Air Data System model and analysis research shows AADL is effective for model-based analysis and specification of complex embedded real-time systems.
AADL supports partial specification which allows modeling and analyzing partial designed system. This flexibility could be used as a coordinating tool in large-scale system development.
Next step research will focus on the AADL reliability and security analyses of embedded real-time system.
